quotes.text: The markets expected the SNB to leave its policy rate unchanged at the monetary policy assessment in December.
Taking into account all available indicators, the effect of monetary policy is expansionary.
Contrary to expectations, inflation declined somewhat in recent months and stood at 0.0% in November.
The SNB expects GDP growth of just under 1.5% for 2025 and around 1% for 2026.
The Governing Board therefore decided to leave the SNB policy rate unchanged at 0%.

fragments.text: Trade tensions as well as concerns about certain segments of the US credit market and the valuation of US technology stocks resulted in temporarily elevated volatility in financial markets.

summary.text: Trade tensions, US credit-market concerns and US technology-stock valuations resulted in temporarily elevated volatility in financial markets.

fragments.text: Taking into account all available indicators, the effect of monetary policy is expansionary.

summary.text: The Governing Board and Alternate Members stated that, taking all available indicators into account, monetary policy's effect is expansionary.

Unemployment is likely to rise further marginally.

summary.text: The SNB expects GDP growth of just under 1.5% for 2025 and around 1% for 2026, while unemployment is likely to rise further marginally.

fragments.text: In light of the outlooks presented with regard to inflation and the economy, the Governing Board determined that monetary conditions are currently appropriate.
The Governing Board therefore decided to leave the SNB policy rate unchanged at 0%.

summary.text: The Governing Board determined that monetary conditions are currently appropriate and decided to leave the SNB policy rate unchanged at 0%.
